messages.content: Implement a Python function from a JSON behavioral card. The card is the only task specification. Return a JSON object with a single string field code containing executable Python source. Define solve with the card's exact signature. Use only Python's standard library. Allowed imports: math, itertools, functools, collections, heapq, bisect, statistics, fractions, operator, typing. Do not import or call NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX or any other third-party library. Do not read files, use network, introspection, eval, exec, input or print. Implement computations yourself using built-ins and the allowed standard library. Return plain JSON-compatible values, not iterators or sets; use string keys in dictionaries. Include any helper functions in the code. No tests or main block. Raise ValueError where the card requires it.

Implement this card:
{
  "algorithm": [
    "Perform a BFS or DFS traversal starting from each unvisited vertex to explore all reachable vertices",
    "Count each distinct connected component found during traversal",
    "The count of such components is the number of connected components in the graph"
  ],
  "constraints": [
    "Vertices are labeled 0 to n-1",
    "Edges are distinct and unordered pairs with u < v",
    "Graph is simple (no self-loops or multiple edges)",
    "The graph may contain isolated vertices",
    "The algorithm must run in O(n + m) time where m is the number of edges"
  ],
  "edge_cases": [
    "n=1 with no edges: returns 1",
    "n=2 with one edge: returns 1",
    "n=2 with no edges: returns 2",
    "n=0 is not allowed (n>=1 per contract)",
    "All vertices isolated: returns n",
    "Graph with one connected component: returns 1"
  ],
  "inputs": "n: integer >= 1; edges: list of distinct [u,v] pairs where 0<=u<v<n",
  "method_id": "networkx.number_connected_components",
  "output": "int: number of connected components (a positive integer)",
  "purpose": "Return the number of connected components in a simple undirected graph with n vertices and edges",
  "signature": "solve(n, edges)"
}
